name: Jordan
headline: Jordan: +2.8% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 84% of GDP
sections: Jordan is a $61.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 93rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $13K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 17.4% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 21.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 38.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 84% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 78% in 2020. The general government balance is −6.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −5.6% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 3.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 76% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 78.0 years (2024). Population: 11.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
